title: Stage 1: What is filling the share?
summary: Get-FolderUsage: size and file count per department folder, biggest first, and an HTML report people can open.

steps.title: Your week on the ops team
body: You have joined the team that keeps the office running. Every week brings the same chores: *the share is full again*,
*the scanner inbox is a mess*, *finance needs the expense totals*. This week you automate them into **OpsKit**, a
module the whole team installs from the feed.
OpsKit lives in `~/src/OpsKit`, laid out like WinOps: `OpsKit.psm1` loads every `Public/*.ps1`, one function per
file. Today: the file share (`~/share`, one folder per department).
**`ConvertTo-Html`** turns objects into an HTML table: a report anyone can open from a mail or a SharePoint page.
Get-Process | Select-Object Name, CPU -First 5 | ConvertTo-Html -Title 'Top processes' | Set-Content top.html

`-Title` sets the page title; `-PreContent '

...

'` adds a heading; `-Head` replaces the whole `` (so
it also replaces `-Title`); `-Fragment` gives only the table, to combine several in one page.

steps.prompt: Why should `Get-FolderUsage` return objects instead of printing a formatted table?
options: So the caller can sort, filter, export to CSV or turn it into HTML: one function, many reports
Format-Table does not work in modules
HTML needs objects with exactly three properties
steps.explain: Keep data and presentation apart: the function returns data, the caller picks `Format-Table` for the screen, `ConvertTo-Html` for a mail, `Export-Csv` for Excel.

steps.title: Get-FolderUsage
prompt: - for each folder **directly** under `-Path`, an object with **`Folder`** (its name), **`Files`** (files in it, all
subfolders included) and **`SizeMB`** (their total size, rounded to one decimal; `0` for an empty folder);

checks.name: Get-FolderUsage ~/share is right
checks.fail: Not quite (see what the check found).

hints: `($files | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum` is `$null` for an empty folder; `[double]$null` is 0.
Output `[pscustomobject]@{ Folder = $_.Name; Files = $files.Count; SizeMB = [math]::Round([double]$bytes / 1MB, 1) }`, then `| Sort-Object SizeMB -Descending`.
solution: Size and file count of each folder directly under -Path, biggest first.
steps.explain: On a real share with millions of files, the slow part is the walk. Run it as a scheduled job at night and keep yesterday's CSV, so the report can also show *growth*, which is what predicts the next full disk.

steps.title: The share report
prompt: Turn the numbers into the report the office manager asked for: **`~/reports/share-usage.html`**, an HTML page
titled **`Share usage`** with a table of every department folder (from `Get-FolderUsage -Path ~/share`).

checks.name: share-usage.html has the table
checks.fail: Not quite (see what the check found).

steps.explain: To mail it: `Send-MailMessage` is obsolete (it cannot do modern authentication); teams use Microsoft Graph (`Send-MgUserMail` in the Microsoft.Graph module) or post the file to a Teams channel webhook with `Invoke-RestMethod`.
